motion.name: action-fill
motion.purpose: Primary-action background only; no hover translation.

motion.name: story-scrub
motion.purpose: ScrollTrigger smoothing in seconds; linear three-segment SVG draw and measured packet path.

motion.name: handset-connector-scrub
motion.purpose: Normal-flow handset map connectors; linear easing and 0.2 stagger.

motion.name: node-highlight
motion.purpose: Timeline-relative duration for CI/server outline highlights; not an autonomous CSS transition.

motion.name: entrance-group
motion.purpose: Explicitly marked offscreen groups only; once at top 88%; rise 26px or side -18px plus opacity and 5% bottom clip; index delay 0.06s capped at 0.18s.

motion.name: entrance-cleanup
motion.purpose: Clear after completion or immediate keyboard-focus reveal; independent matchMedia cleanup restores reduced-motion static content.

motion.name: halftone-swell
motion.purpose: CSS transforms directly painted column groups from -14 to +14 SVG units; negative phase delay -x/1440*6s. Desktop/mobile run only while visible, tab-active, motion-permitted and not user-paused.

extensions.previewNotes: Tonal ramps are synthetic OKLCH panel previews only. Component snippets show static semantic states, not the site enhancement handlers or GSAP timeline. Actual root CSS variables and self-hosted fonts are required. The story preview represents the readable static fallback; no input field exists.

contrast.method: WCAG relative sRGB luminance; rounded ratios, not a full accessibility audit.

elevation.method: Tonal layering only; no shadows or glow.
elevation.entranceOwnership: Entrance wrappers never animate the sticky diagram’s scrubbed properties.

scrollStage.purpose: Contained scroll explanation only; not a global control-radius replacement.
scrollStage.layout: Desktop outer min(1456px, calc(100% - 48px)); inner min(1280px, calc(100% - 96px)); 72px/64px vertical padding, 48px heading separation. Up to 700px: outer 8px/inner 16px per side, 48px vertical padding, 35px heading separation.
scrollStage.decoration: Both authored inline SVG fields contain directly painted wave column groups, not defs/use instances; aria-hidden, nonfocusable and pointer-transparent. Only decoration clips; stage overflow stays visible.
scrollStage.placement: First decorative SVG sticks at top96px only for min-width900px and no-preference motion. Smaller screens remain in normal placement but animate while visible; reduced motion is static. No canvas loop or pointer response.
scrollStage.stickyInvariant: Keep existing diagram pinning and final narrative ::after real-flow spacer unchanged.

wave.control: Native translated pause/resume button; min-height44px, deep fill, light ink, 4px corners and 8px12px padding; hidden without ready non-reduced enhancement.
wave.gating: IntersectionObserver, document visibility and reduced-motion preference gate CSS play state. Explicit pause choice survives offscreen/reentry.
wave.fallback: Missing base-client JavaScript or IntersectionObserver, or reduced motion, leaves a static field and hides the animation-only control. Deferred GSAP import/failure/teardown does not own or disable the independently initialized wave.
wave.paintInvariant: Directly painted SVG column groups in both fields. Computed transforms on defs/use source groups did not prove visible movement; regression evidence compares actual rendered dot pixels.
wave.ownership: The base client initializes setupWave independently. Wave owns only dot-column transforms; deferred GSAP owns the scrubbed story and its separate entrance controller. No story lifecycle teardown owns wave state.

favicon.geometry: Exact canonical four9.5×9.5 rectangles, rx1.2, at5.5/17 coordinates within a32×32 viewBox; rotate(45 16 16).
favicon.provenance: Adaptive CSS/class derivative of the original geometry, not a byte-identical source copy. Does not replace the separate visible page-mark asset.

motionLoading.story: Dynamic GSAP/story import is gated by permitted motion and a one-shot IntersectionObserver with rootMargin "200px 0px". It disconnects once the story approaches. If IntersectionObserver is unavailable, use immediate permitted-motion fallback.
motionLoading.wave: Lightweight setupWave initializes from the base client independently of GSAP proximity/import/teardown. Existing6s ±14-unit CSS wave and pause/visibility/preference gating are unchanged.
motionLoading.fallback: Essential story and entrance content starts visible and remains static during delayed/failed GSAP loading; wave retains its own readiness and gating. No performance score or Lighthouse outcome is implied.

narrative.overview:
The Naval Workshop preserves the existing QuadShip identity: precise compartment geometry, expanded industrial lettering and legible humanist reading text. The independent marketing site extends that world; it does not redesign the application or rewrite its source documents.

The user-directed dark canvas remains a slightly lighter interpretation of the supplied #12233A. Large explanatory diagrams now carry the composition, with distinct deep, reading and raised planes, fine structural rules and focused warm action signals. The reference-led composition remains intact; the latest refinement adds selective grouped entrances without reviving a generic global section observer.
keyCharacteristics: Original four-compartment diamond and lowercase wordmark.
Expanded Archivo paired with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.
Deep, reading and raised naval planes with focused warm actions.
Large causal diagrams with native-scroll enhancement and complete static fallbacks.

rules.name: The Scarce Oxide Rule
rules.body: Use warm oxide to prioritize real primary actions, one large hero headline line, focus and causal highlights. Keep broad planes naval; use the lighter accent-copy role for small warm text on raised surfaces.

rules.name: The Original Lockup Rule
rules.body: Keep the original rotated compartment geometry and lowercase quadship lockup; use QuadShip in prose.

rules.name: The Compartment Rule
rules.body: Separate regions through tonal contrast and fine rules, never shadows.

rules.name: The Decorative Clip Rule
rules.body: Clip only the scroll-stage decoration, never the stage or its content; preserve visible overflow and the final narrative’s real-flow spacer so native sticky behavior survives.

dos: Do preserve the canonical mark geometry and bundled variable fonts.
Do use deep navy labels on warm primary actions and the lighter accent-copy role for small warm text on raised planes.
Do pair state colors with text and distinct SVG shapes.
Do keep content visible without JavaScript and complete without motion.
Do preserve Spanish as the static default and switch English in place on the same URL.
donts: Don't treat illustrative application screens or CI diagrams as shipped product interfaces.
Don't replace the existing identity with provisional cobalt/peach styling.
Don't introduce shadows, large oxide fields, uncontrolled or unpausable perpetual motion, or scroll hijacking.
Don't create localized routes or claim separate English indexing.
Don't modify the original application or its brand and product documents as part of this website system.
